bullets.title: May NFP blows past estimates at +172k; labor market reaccelerates, hawkish for rates
bullets.body: May nonfarm payrolls came in at +172k vs ~88k consensus, with prior two months revised up a cumulative +93k, pushing the 3-month average to +188k — well above any 2025 monthly print. Unemployment ticked down to 4.296%, prime-age EPOP near cycle high. AHE rose +0.32% MoM; YoY wage growth edged down to 3.4%. Multiple desks flagged the print as decisively hawkish: data now moves against any Fed rate-cut thesis, with markets pricing ~1 full hike by year-end and ~40-50% probability of a 2-4 hike cycle per some strategists.

bullets.title: Fed easing bias removal expected in June; 2s/10s flattening, 10yr at 4.53%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects the Fed to remove its easing bias at the June FOMC meeting following the payrolls beat. The 10-year yield jumped to ~4.53% post-print, with 2s10s continuing to flatten toward one-year lows. Strategists are targeting 2yr and 10yr at 5% and 30yr at 6%, while some flagged that payrolls above 120k are now viewed as risk-off given inflation — not growth — as the primary constraint.

bullets.title: ECB almost certain to hike 25bp next week; additional hike by September likely
bullets.body: JPMorgan and 22V Research both flag near-certain 25bp ECB hike at next week's meeting, with a hawkish signal pointing to a total of three hikes. Eurozone core CPI jumped to 2.5% YoY in May vs. a March baseline of 2.2%, and Iran-driven energy prices keep TTF near €50/MW. A further hike in September is base case; JPM sees risk skewing slightly toward three total hikes. Separately, Eurozone Q1 GDP came in at -0.2% QoQ and +0.3% YoY, both missing the +0.1%/+0.8% consensus.

bullets.title: SOX most overbought since 1999-2000; semis down 2-6% pre-market on AVGO soft guidance
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks were broadly lower pre-market: ARM -6%, NVDA -1.9%, MRVL/MU -4%, SNDK/AVGO -2%, INTC -3.8%. AVGO's soft Wednesday night guidance triggered the AI-sector selloff; SOX had closed ~75% above its 200-dma on Wednesday, the most extended level since 1999-2000. Multiple strategists flagged bubble-like price action in SOX and KOSPI (SK Hynix -10% overnight), though broad market froth is not yet consensus. Tech is now 39.7% of S&P 500, nearly 5pp above the March 2000 peak.

bullets.title: Citi Bear Market Checklist at 10/18 globally; BofA Bull & Bear in deep sell-signal territory
bullets.body: Citi flags global stocks at frothiest valuations since 2008 with 10 of 18 bear-market risk indicators triggered, citing elevated sentiment, AI-driven spending, and IPO surge. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sits at 8.7, deep in sell-signal territory, with equity inflows slowing and credit inflows surging. 22V Research echoes that bubble price action is real in select stocks and indexes, but sees no broad market bubble — favoring energy, rails, and KRE while targeting Bitcoin at $40k.

bullets.title: Iran fires warning shots at US Navy in Gulf of Oman; Hormuz closure risk re-priced
bullets.body: Iran's navy fired warning shots at US destroyers in the Gulf of Oman, and the Iranian FM warned American bases are legitimate targets. Rosneft CEO warned no country can replace Middle East oil supply and flagged $150/bbl risk if the Strait of Hormuz closes. NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index remained elevated at 1.77 in May despite a slight dip; Drewry container shipping index surged 23% WoW to $3,433/40ft.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO set for next Friday at $135/share, $75B raise; largest IPO in history
bullets.body: SpaceX is holding firm at $135/share (already oversubscribed) for a $75B equity raise targeting a $1.77T valuation, with the IPO set for Friday June 12. China and Hong Kong investors are barred on national security grounds. Morgan Stanley projects SpaceX revenue reaching $3.4T and adjusted EBITDA of $2.7T by 2040. The IPO is expected to trigger ~$30B in passive inflows, likely pulling capital from mega-cap tech, and creates a rising overhang for telecom/cable (Wolfe: telecom sub-sector down -13.2% YTD vs S&P +10.8%).

bullets.title: Jefferies raises CoWoS forecasts; TSM wafer pricing to rise 10%+ for all customers in 2027
bullets.body: Jefferies raises CoWoS capacity forecasts to 180k wpm by end-2027 (from 170k) and 220k by end-2028, with NVDA holding 50%+ allocation at 10mn+ GPU volumes. TSM's supply-demand gap is widening to 15-20% as server CPU demand surges, driving 10%+ wafer price increases for all customers in 2027 (except Apple at 1-2% in 2026). AVGO's allocation was revised down to 24-25% from 28.5% in 2027, but TPU volumes remain robust at 6.2mn.

bullets.title: Jefferies flow data: infrastructure software and memory seeing net buying; defensives bleeding
bullets.body: Jefferies desk flow analysis shows hedge funds and long-only investors net buying infrastructure software, memory, and analog semis. TXN's upside beat with above-seasonal guides spurred analog semi buying. Long-only investors sold Software for 9 straight weeks in early 2025 but Application Software saw one of the highest sigma HF moves on a recent Monday. Defensive sectors (cable, telcos) experiencing notable outflows as the AI trade rally continues.

bullets.title: Risk-on positioning back to pre-pandemic highs; short index vol exposure vulnerable
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag that risk-on positioning has rebounded to pre-pandemic highs, signaling renewed appetite for growth/high-beta assets. Three-month implied correlations are at five-year lows, leaving short index vol positions vulnerable to shocks. OPCO desk targets a mid-June pullback of -3% to -5% S&P and -15% to -20% in semis around the CPI/SpaceX/FOMC/Opex catalyst cluster (June 10, 12, 17, 18).

bullets.title: ORCL CapEx guide and $25B equity raise are next week's key tech catalyst; ADBE also reports
bullets.body: ORCL reports Wednesday after close with consensus FY27 CapEx at $61.2B (~22% YoY ramp) and focus on updates to its $25B equity raise. ADBE reports Thursday after close. Fed officials Hammack and Logan signaled higher rates may be needed to combat inflation, consistent with market pricing of near-100% probability of hold at June FOMC but 14bp of hikes priced through year-end.

bullets.title: Foxconn May revenue +39.6% YoY; Q2 tracking 'well above' prior significant growth guidance
bullets.body: Foxconn reported May revenue of NT$859.4B (US$27.3B), up 39.6% YoY — the 3rd best month ever — driven by AI server assembly and iPhone production. Management said Q2 is tracking 'well above previously anticipated significant growth,' providing a positive read-through for AI server supply chain names.

bullets.title: Data center supply deficit widening to 12 GW in 2025; power and labor as binding constraints
bullets.body: Jefferies data center REIT analyst estimates ~21 GW demand vs <9 GW delivered in 2025, creating a 12 GW structural deficit. Hyperscaler capex surges to $770B in 2026E (+74% YoY) with a $2T backlog. Labor is the binding constraint in 2026; cooling becomes binding from 2028. EQIX and DLR benefit from existing permitted/powered footprints; Switch private fundraise values the company at $50B+, materially above public REIT multiples. Former crypto miners (CORZ, WULF, HUT) are converting to AI/HPC at compressed timelines.

bullets.title: MU options traded $1.5B premium — exceeding SPY and QQQ combined — as stock lost $94B market cap
bullets.body: Micron options notional premium of ~$1.5B exceeded SPY (~$1B) and QQQ (~$1B) combined on Thursday, even as MU's market cap fell ~$94B — a greater than 1-standard-deviation move for a top-20 stock. Separately, Jensen Huang certified Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix as qualified HBM4 suppliers. SK Hynix fell nearly 10% overnight (KOSPI), flagged as a potential 'first crack' in the crowded semiconductor trade.

bullets.title: Eurozone GDP missed badly; BoE hike seen in July if oil stays above $100; UK borrowing outlook darkens
bullets.body: Eurozone Q1 GDP contracted -0.2% QoQ vs +0.1% consensus; YoY growth decelerated to 0.3% vs 0.8% expected. JPMorgan expects the BoE to hike in July if oil remains above $100 into Q3; BoE member Greene appears ready to vote for a June hike. UK CPI expectations sit at 3.7% per the BoE DMP survey, with wage growth picking up to 4.3%.

bullets.title: Anthropic calls for global AI development pause as models near recursive self-improvement
bullets.body: Anthropic urged a global pause in AI development, citing AI models approaching the capability to improve themselves without human intervention. Separately, MS TMT notes Anthropic's Claude Mythos is achieving 52x speedup on training tasks and 8x code merge rate in Q2 2026 vs 2024. The Obernolte-Trahan AI Act draft was flagged as net positive for AI infrastructure (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSMC) but mixed-negative for frontier model developers.

bullets.title: BofA: US jobless rate/CPI alignment at 4.2% would be only the 7th such instance since 1960
bullets.body: Michael Hartnett at BofA notes that if the US jobless rate falls to 4.2% or below — aligned with expected CPI next week around 4.2% — it would mark only the 7th such co-occurrence since 1960, with prior instances in 1966, 1973, 1990, and 2000. All prior instances preceded significant macro regime shifts, flagging elevated risk for current positioning.

bullets.title: Gold breaking 200-dma signals deleveraging; retail demand disappears at support
bullets.body: Gold is breaking below its 200-day moving average, flagged by multiple strategists as a signal of deleveraging and tightening financial conditions. 22V Research expects gold and silver to work lower as rates rise. Retail sentiment in gold has reversed sharply — demand peaked at highs and is now absent at support levels, consistent with procyclical behavior.

bullets.title: Supply chain stress intensifying: container costs +23% WoW; NY Fed index still elevated at 1.77
bullets.body: Drewry World Container Index jumped 23% in one week to $3,433 per 40-foot container, consistent with supply chain re-stress driven by Iran/Hormuz tensions. NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index dipped slightly to 1.77 in May but remains elevated. Q1 unit labor costs were revised down to +1.8% from +2.3%, and productivity was trimmed to +0.3%, suggesting limited domestic cost-push, but external logistics inflation is re-accelerating.

bullets.title: JPMorgan upgrades TSLA to Neutral from Underweight; raises PT to $475 on robotics/AI thesis
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded Tesla from Underweight to Neutral and raised its price target to $475 from $145, shifting the thesis away from near-term EV earnings to autonomous driving, robotics, AI, and software upside. The upgrade represents a significant capitulation from JPM's long-standing bearish stance.
